title: Whence Do Our Mournful Thoughts Arise
description: Whence Do Our Mournful Thoughts Arise in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 32, headed “Strength from heaven, Isa. 40. 27-30”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Whence do our mourn-ful thoughts a-rise? And where's our cou-rage fled? Has rest-less sin and rag-ing hell Struck all our com-forts dead?

lines: Whence do our mournful thoughts arise?
Has restless sin and raging hell
Have we forgot th' almighty Name
That form'd the earth and sea?
He gives the conquest to the weak,
And treads their foes to hell.
Mere mortal power shall fade and die,
But we that wait upon the Lord
The saints shall mount on eagles' wings

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
